Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock rebounded 7.79% on Monday after the chipmaker's shares experienced a rough couple of days last week. The rally of AMD stock came alongside praise from one of Wall Street's top analysts. Five-star Bernstein analyst Mark Newman reiterated a Buy rating and a $650 price target for AMD stock, implying a possible 43.74% upside.

Newman came out to support AMD after the company was targeted in a short report last week. Hunterbrook was behind this report and claimed that AMD has continued to provide support for GPUs that belong to blacklisted Chinese companies. However, AMD claimed that this report misrepresented its practices. While investors were rattled by that report, a continued bullish stance from a top Wall Street analyst appears to have boosted morale today.

Should Investors Trust Newman on AMD?

Newman is a highly-ranked analyst on TipRanks, placing 209 out of 12,607 Wall Street analysts. He is also ranked 1,112 out of 37,861 experts on the platform. His Success Rate is 59%, with 42 out of 71 ratings generating a profit. The analyst also has an Average Return of 37.4% per rating.

Newman is an analyst that is heavily focused on the computer hardware sector. Other stocks in this sector that he covers include Nvidia (NVDA), Intel (INTC), Broadcom (AVGO), SanDisk (SNDK), Western Digital (WDC), and Seagate (STX).

What Other News Is Affecting AMD Stock Today?

In a major surprise, Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang will return as the company's CEO. He resigned earlier this month following allegations of extramarital affairs, including one affair with a possible Chinese spy, as reported by TipRanks. His departure shocked the tech sector, putting pressure on AI stocks.

With Huang's return as Nvidia's CEO, AI and tech stocks were on the rise today. AMD was among them, as the rival semiconductor company extends a 98.16% year-to-date rally. Investors will also note that shares of AMD have gained 97.35% over the past 12 months.

Is AMD Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for AMD is Strong Buy, based on 28 Buy and three Hold ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average AMD stock price target of $652.26, suggesting a possible 40.79% upside for the company's shares. (See AMD Stock Forecast)

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), an AI and CPU chips provider, closed at $453.46, up 6.85%. Shares rose after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, and investors are watching AI-chip sentiment and conference commentary.
Trading volume reached 53.0M shares, coming in about 93% above its three-month average of 27.5M shares.

How the markets moved today

S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) closed at 7,237, up 4.73%, while Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) closed at 24,090, up 6.51%. Among semiconductors and semiconductor equipment peers, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) closed at $165.05, up 31.48%, and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) closed at $59.66, up 16.34%, highlighting a broad AI-chip rebound.

What this means for investors

AMD was one of the many stocks that benefited from the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO. This stands in contrast to what happened Friday when AMD stock plunged on a short-seller report. The report alleged that some AMD server firmware fell into the hands of a blacklisted Chinese company.

By today, that report appeared to be forgotten. Although AMD is a major competitor to Nvidia in the data center space, it benefits indirectly as Huang's return breathes new life into the AI trade and brings stability to the semiconductor sector.

Fortunately, AMD has made technical progress to the point that it may benefit directly as well. Many industry analysts believe that AMD's MI450 series GPU (along with the MI455X Helios rack) has, at least on paper, caught up to Nvidia's latest release, the Vera Rubin.

Admittedly, at a P/E ratio of 98, the tech stock remains far more expensive than Nvidia, which, even with its gains today, trades at just 18 times earnings. However, analysts forecast that AMD's revenue will grow at 51% annually this year, then rise to 84% in 2027.

Amid a reinvigorated AI trade, such growth gives investors all the more reason to take a closer look at AMD stock.

title: ASML Stock’s Sell-Off Looks Excessive Against Its Growth Outlook
detail:
ASML Stock’s Sell-Off Looks Excessive Against Its Growth Outlook

ASML Holding's (ASML) stock sell-off looks excessive against its growth outlook, in my view. The lithography equipment manufacturer reported record quarterly sales of €11.7 billion in Q3 2026. During the earnings call, CEO Christophe Fouquet said planned supply for 2027 and 2028 "will not fully meet the demand of our customers." That is a striking message during a semiconductor sell-off.

While investors are questioning how long the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout can last, ASML's customers are already asking for more equipment years ahead. Given that disconnect, I think the decline offers an unusually attractive entry point. Thus, my rating on ASML stock is a Buy.

The Sell-Off Overlooks ASML's Position

The ongoing, brutal market sell-off likely overlooks ASML's position within semiconductor manufacturing. Investors worry that enormous AI spending could produce disappointing returns. Possible data-center overbuilding and tighter export controls have only added to the pressure. As a result, ASML has been caught squarely in the broader sector retreat, pushing the stock 32% below its 52-week high.

I believe these concerns deserve attention. However, what the market fails to see is that ASML has more protection than many individual chip companies.

ASML is the only manufacturer of Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems, which print the finest features on advanced chips. That monopoly insulates the company from the fierce competition among chip designers. Nvidia (NVDA) could lose share to AMD (AMD) or a hyperscaler's custom processor. However, the manufacturers producing those competing chips would still need ASML's equipment.

Increasing chip complexity also means more lithography work. The eventual winner among chip designers matters less than continued demand for advanced manufacturing. The most recent Q3 results supported that distinction. Net income reached €5 billion, even if that included a €500 million Mistral AI valuation gain. Gross margin exceeded guidance at 57.5%.

Installed Base Management sales also beat expectations at €3.3 billion, helped by productivity upgrades. Looking further ahead, the demand picture is even stronger. Customer forecasts keep increasing, and planned supply remains insufficient for 2027 and 2028. Some customers are discussing orders for 2029 and 2030. I find those conversations more persuasive than the sector's current mood.

Why Does AMD Trade at 30x When Nvidia Is at 10x Forward Earnings? AMD's China Exposure Is Bigger ©@Alexander's Images via Canva, @Nicolas Foster from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Nvidia stock jumped 31% today after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, lifting its forward P/E off a three-year low of 8.7x.

AMD trades at well over twice Nvidia's forward P/E and Intel even higher, though Dan Niles's figures put AMD's revenue growth only about 10 points ahead of Nvidia's.

22.4% of AMD's revenue is billed in China and Hong Kong, more than twice Nvidia's share.

The tests for AMD's premium are a Helios customer's 2027 spending plan in late January and AMD's fourth-quarter report.

Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) stock jumped 31% today after its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and a director, effective immediately. He had resigned on Nov. 12.

The news comes in the middle of an argument investors have been having for days. In a post on the r/ValueInvesting subreddit, one investor asked why Nvidia sat near 8x forward earnings while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD:NASDAQ) and Intel (INTC:NASDAQ) "still trade at 30x forward."

The more you dig into it, the stranger AMD's premium looks.

The poster has the multiples about right

At the last close, TIKR had AMD at 28.2x forward earnings and Nvidia at 8.7x. Today's jump puts Nvidia back above 10x.

Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, put Nvidia at "11x CY27 PE for projected 70% revenue growth," against AMD "at 30x for projected 80%+ revenue growth," in a reply on X. On his figures, investors pay nearly 3x as much for each dollar of AMD's earnings, in return for about 10 more points of revenue growth.

Intel is the starker case, at "34x PE for just 11% estimated revenue growth." Growth alone can't explain chip multiples like these.

TIKR tracks 54 analysts on AMD. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on AMD, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See AMD's Analyst Ratings

AMD is priced for a huge 2027

What investors are paying for is AMD's next two years. Analysts expect its normalized EPS to nearly double in 2026, then more than double again in 2027:

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2027 (TIKR)

Analysts haven't cut that 2027 estimate since Hunterbrook's report, either.

The 2027 jump depends on Helios, AMD's rack-scale system. Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) has made a binding commitment for the first gigawatt of a deal for up to 6 gigawatts. Every gigawatt Meta puts on Helios is one Nvidia doesn't fill.

On China, AMD has more at stake

On Nov. 19, Hunterbrook Media, whose affiliated fund is short AMD, reported that 22.4% of AMD's revenue is billed to customers in China and Hong Kong, against 9.1% for Nvidia.

Today's big story: Reported SEC Probe: Could Nvidia Stock Fall To $92?

Update, Nov 23: TSMC rose about 16% in Monday morning trading, to about $369, as chip stocks jumped after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. The figures below are at Friday's close. At about $369, the stock is still about 24% below its Oct 5 record close, while its sales keep rising.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) fell 9.5% on Friday, Nov 20, from $352.09 to $318.71. That capped a 20.1% drop for the week. Our Nov 20 piece covered Thursday, when TSMC took one of the hardest hits as stocks fell on AI worries. For the record of past drops from Thursday's $352.09 close, see Holding TSMC Near $352? Past Drops Went Deeper.

This piece asks what would warn of a TSMC revenue fall like 2001's. The short answer is monthly sales reports that come in below a year earlier. That has not happened. TSMC's October 2026 revenue was up 59.7% from October 2025.

History also shows the stock moves first. In each of TSMC's three past revenue declines, the stock peaked well before sales fell. At Friday's close, the stock was 34.4% below its record close of $485.80 on Monday, Oct 5. So far, that is a falling price with rising sales.

How long did the stock fall before sales did?

We compare revenue year on year. That means a period's sales against the same period a year earlier. On that basis, TSMC's annual revenue has fallen in only three years since 1997. Those years were 2001, 2009 and 2023.

We counted each decline the same way. The count starts at the stock's peak. It stops at the first quarter with revenue below the same quarter a year earlier. That took 5 quarters in 2001, 2 in 2008-09 and 5 in 2023.

By the end of that first down quarter, the stock had already dropped a long way. It was 60.3% below its peak in 2001, 29.9% in 2008 and 26.1% in 2023. The price drop came well before the sales drop.

TSMC dropped 20.1% in one week, and its sales have not even turned down yet. If a big part of your savings rides on this one stock, a slide like 2001's would be a long one to sit through.
